t: You're looking at the Jewel Tower, a 14th-century survivor of the Palace of Westminster. It was built in 1365 and 1366 to hold the personal treasure of King Edward III. Originally a three-storey, crenellated stone building, it stood in a secluded part of the palace, protected by a moat linked to the Thames. Henry Yevele, the king's master mason from 1360, designed it, and he is also credited with commissioning it. The ground floor has elaborate sculpted vaulting, which one historian calls an architectural masterpiece. Royal treasure was stored here until a fire in 1512 moved Henry VIII to Whitehall.
